function_analysis: Unchanged: lower mean wall shear at cruising speed versus a clean foul-release coating, biocide-free fouling control, 3-5 year durability, no large consumption, hull-scale application. The map shows that compliance-based concepts deliver fouling-release (stress) benefits, not friction benefits; the stress-governed cells are where honest simulated gains exist, and their main open issue is mechanical robustness of soft layers (cleaning brushes, fenders, debris).

requirements.name: low_friction_drag
requirements.criterion: Reduces the mean wall shear stress / frictional resistance at cruising speed versus a clean, standard foul-release hull coating.

requirements.name: non_toxic_antifouling
requirements.criterion: Prevents fouling settlement or makes it release easily without releasing biocides, heavy metals or other toxic substances into the sea.

requirements.name: multi_year_seawater_durability
requirements.criterion: Keeps its function and adhesion for at least 3-5 years in seawater (hydrolysis, abrasion, UV at the waterline, cleaning).

requirements.name: low_consumption_operation
requirements.criterion: Needs no continuous supply of material or energy that is large compared with the fuel it saves, and no frequent reapplication.

requirements.name: hull_scale_applicability
requirements.criterion: Can be applied to large steel hull areas with dry-dock methods at a cost comparable to premium hull coatings.

mechanism_classes_considered: graded_stiffness (crust load spreading, armour over soft foundation)
interfacial_slip (hydration lubrication at the fouling/coating interface)
analogues_considered: Pack ice and nilas crust distributing point loads onto the slush below (ice-load spreading, Winkler/Pasternak foundation)
Hydration lubrication of articular cartilage and fish mucus (lubricin, zwitterionic brushes; friction coefficients 1e-3 to 1e-4)

Anti-slip deck coatings with broadcast aggregate

candidates.title: Pack-ice crust load spreading against brush damage
candidates.summary: A 0.3 mm stiff, tough crust (G ~ 5 MPa, fibre-reinforced silicone-PU) over a 2.5 mm soft graded gel, dimensioned like sea-ice crust over slush so that it spreads concentrated point loads (cleaning-brush bristles, sand, debris edges, barnacle base edges) over a much larger gel area. The peak stress in the soft gel, which otherwise tears under in-water hull grooming, drops several-fold, while the gel keeps the coating compliant for fouling release.

back_of_envelope.quantity: Reduction of peak normal stress in the soft gel under a bristle point load, versus the uncrusted gel; drag change ~0%
back_of_envelope.formula: Pasternak foundation: spreading length l = sqrt(G_c*t_c/k) with k = E_gel/t_gel = 1.8e5/2.5e-3 = 7.2e7 Pa/m, G_c t_c = 5e6*3e-4 = 1500 N/m -> l = 4.6 mm; a bristle line load over a width a = 0.3 mm is spread over ~2l = 9 mm -> peak gel stress down by ~2l/a ~ 30x (thin line load); for broad fender contacts (a >> l) no reduction. Friction versus a clean foul-release coating: 0%.

candidates.main_risk: A stiffer crust raises the surface stiffness felt by small foulers and by the peel front, eroding the fouling-release benefit of the gel; the concept only helps against point loads, not blunt fender impacts.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: the nilas-crust elite (thin 0.15 mm, soft crust) and two-layer foul-release systems. New: the crust is dimensioned as a load-spreading plate by ice-mechanics (Pasternak) theory, specifically to make soft foul-release coatings survive in-water grooming, which is otherwise their main incompatibility.
candidates.baseline: The same soft graded gel coating without load-spreading crust (and, for release, a standard clean silicone foul-release coating)
candidates.inspiration_source: Sea-ice crust over slush distributing loads (ice-bearing capacity on a soft foundation)
candidates.physical_mechanism: A shear-stiff crust on an elastic foundation spreads a concentrated surface load: G_c t_c w'' - k w = -q(x), with the interface normal stress k*w. The crust stiffness sets the spreading length l = sqrt(G_c t_c/k); the peak gel stress falls roughly as a/(2l) for loads narrower than l. Steady model: 1D Pasternak ODE over a half-span with a load strip at the centre (source term) and decayed far field.

candidates.title: Cartilage-style hydration-lubricated release interphase
candidates.summary: A self-stratifying coating in which zwitterionic (sulfobetaine) block copolymers anchored in a byssus-like graded PU-silicone interphase form a ~50 nm hydration-lubrication layer at the surface, like lubricin on cartilage. Barnacle and mussel cement that lands on it sits on a water-bearing, sliding interface, so fouling slides off under a much lower shear stress; abraded brush chains are replaced from the bulk reservoir as the surface wears.

back_of_envelope.quantity: Reduction of the shear stress needed to slide adhered fouling off, versus a standard silicone foul-release coating; drag change ~0%
back_of_envelope.formula: Barnacle shear release on silicone foul release ~0.05-0.1 MPa (ASTM D5618-type). A hydration-lubricated interface carries shear by the viscous hydration layer: tau = mu_eff*v/h with mu_eff ~ 1e3*mu_water (confined water) = 1 Pa s, h = 5e-9 m, creep speed v ~ 1e-6 m/s -> tau ~ 200 Pa (sliding), but cement penetrates part of the brush: take a 30-50% reduction of release stress as realistic; value 0 for friction.

candidates.main_risk: Fouling cements (DOPA, barnacle cement proteins) displace hydration water and bind to the brush itself, so the lubricated interface may never form under real adhesives; and the reservoir depletes within a few years of abrasion.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: zwitterionic antifouling coatings (settlement resistance) and amphiphilic foul-release coatings. New: the brush is used as a hydration-lubricated slip interface to lower the release shear of already attached fouling (cartilage mechanism), combined with a byssus-graded, self-replenishing reservoir interphase for multi-year life.
candidates.baseline: Clean, standard silicone foul-release hull coating (release shear of barnacles ~0.05-0.1 MPa)
candidates.inspiration_source: Articular cartilage hydration lubrication (lubricin/phosphatidylcholine) and mussel byssus graded interphase
candidates.physical_mechanism: Under a fouling organism's base, shear stress is transmitted through a nm hydration layer whose effective slip lowers the interfacial shear; the organism detaches by sliding once the hydrodynamic shear exceeds this low release stress. Steady model: shear transfer through the base of an adherend over a slipping interface (shear-lag with a slip-reduced interface stiffness), giving the peak interfacial shear for a given hydrodynamic load; lower interface stiffness means lower peak and longer transfer length.

candidates.title: Broadcast-scree silicone-capped armour coating
candidates.summary: Instead of laid tiles, 1 mm hard ceramic beads are broadcast into a wet 1.5 mm soft silicone foundation (like anti-slip deck aggregate or scree embedded in fines) and overcoated with a 100 um smooth silicone foul-release skin. The beads carry fender, cleaning and debris loads and stop gouges at the skin depth; the fouler sees a low-energy silicone surface over a compliant foundation, fixing the elite's weak point (hard, high-adhesion tile surface) and its laborious tiling.

back_of_envelope.quantity: Change of mean wall shear at 7 m/s versus a clean standard silicone foul-release coating (plus release stress as secondary benefit)
back_of_envelope.formula: Overcoat levels bead waviness to amplitude ~5-10 um over 1-2 mm wavelength (slope < 1%): k+ ~ 1 -> hydraulically smooth -> friction change 0 +/- 0.5%. Release: C = t_f/G_f + t_skin/G_skin = 1.5e-3/2e5 + 1e-4/3.3e5 = 7.8e-9 m/Pa, w_a = 0.05 -> sigma_c = sqrt(0.1/7.8e-9) = 3.6 kPa vs 10.5 kPa (-65%), where the parent reached only -15%.

candidates.main_risk: Beads locally stiffen the surface where the skin is thin over a bead crest, creating hard spots that barnacles use as anchors, and bead waviness may exceed the hydraulically smooth limit if the overcoat is thin.
candidates.novelty_vs_known: Closest: the desert-pavement elite (laid hard tiles, hard surface) and anti-slip deck coatings (exposed aggregate). New: broadcast, overcoated hard aggregate inside a soft foul-release system, so the load-bearing armour sits below a low-energy compliant skin and the whole system is sprayable/broadcast in a dry dock.
candidates.baseline: Clean, standard silicone foul-release hull coating (~0.3 mm, E ~ 1 MPa) at 7 m/s
candidates.inspiration_source: Scree and armoured sediment beds: coarse clasts embedded in fine, soft matrix
candidates.physical_mechanism: Hard beads embedded in a soft foundation form a discontinuous armour layer below the surface: blunt loads are carried bead-to-bead into the foundation, limiting indentation and gouge depth to about the skin thickness, while between contacts the compliance of the foundation plus skin sets the release stress. Flow sees a smooth, overcoated surface. Steady model: 1D shear deformation through foundation and skin in series (release compliance) or sublayer shear over the smooth wall.
